pr_title: Bluetooth: host: Retry failed auto-initiated phy request
pr_body:
An auto-initiated phy request may fail and consequently the correct
phy is not set, and the auto-initiation is stalled. This is preventing
the DLE procedure from being executed.

This commit introduces a limited retry mechanism which handles the
following error cases:

1) An error occurs when preparing the link layer request. Phy update
is not sent. This is typically a BT_HCI_ERR_CMD_DISALLOWED error due
to LLCP state machine busy.

2) Central rejects phy update request with a "Different Transaction
Collision".

In both cases a delayed retry is needed to request phy update when
ongoing procedure is completed.

Fixes #31473.

Signed-off-by: Morten Priess <mtpr@oticon.com>
pr_comments: Btw, I'm surprised it's the responsibility of the host to do this extra work. I'd have expected the controller to handle it.

> Btw, I'm surprised it's the responsibility of the host to do this extra work. I'd have expected the controller to handle it.

Well i might also seem counter-intuitive that the host should do this, especially in this case where both host and controller are Zephyr, but what about the the case where the controller is just another blackbox, what would be the logic then? Would it make sense to stall the auto-initiation just because an "unexpected" BT_HCI_ERR_CMD_DISALLOWED was received.

I think we maybe should look at this as two use cases. One is where the interface function returns an error. As the auto-initiate feature is implemented in the host, this is where we have to deal with that error.
The other is where the phy update initiates without error. Here you could argue that the controller should do any necessary retry, and just delay the "complete" notification to host.

@mtpr-ot Is the problem that the DLE procedures is not done, or that the auto-phy update does not end up with the PHY that you wanted?
I think the solution to the problem of the DLE procedure is to remove this initiation of the procedures one at a time and submit them all to the controller insetad (like DLE and conn-param-update-request). The controller should be able to handle them all as pending now AFAIK.

> @mtpr-ot Is the problem that the DLE procedures is not done, or that the auto-phy update does not end up with the PHY that you wanted?

See #31473. Both are problems causing instrument malfunction for us. There are workarounds to be implemented at app level, but until convinced of otherwise, I think the issues should fixed within the host- and/or controller.

@mtpr Can you please check if the issue you described is actually happening on current master, there has been many changes to the LLCP procedures since 2.2.1 I think. BT_HCI_ERR_CMD_DISALLOWED should not happen anymore, if it does it should be handled in the controller in my opinion.

Since the controller can handle multiple LLCP procedures pending the sequential initiation of the control procedures could be removed.

> @mtpr-ot
> 
> > what is your comment to changing the controller to defer instead of returning "disallowed"?
> 
> Identified a bug in controller that prevented PHY update from being cached. Have now sent #31570 to remove returning disallowed.

With that merged, can we close #31473 ?

> With that merged, can we close #31473 ?

We still need a fix for the "Different Transaction Collision".
@mtpr-ot will you follow-up with this PR so we can close  #31473?

> @mtpr-ot will you follow-up with this PR so we can close #31473?

With the solution deemed outside of host responsibility, we need a controller solution. This PR will not cover that, so I'm closing this PR.

issue_context.title: Failed phy request not retried and may prevent DLE procedure during auto-initiation
issue_context.body:
When an auto-initiated phy request collides with other procedure initiated by the peer, the "Different Transaction Collision" error code is ignored, and auto-initiation continued, effectively skipping phy update.

**To Reproduce**
After connection is established, the central/peripheral LLCP timing must be such that the auto-initiated phy update request from peripheral is sent just **before** e.g. a encryption request is received by the peripheral. This will get the request in the air, and central responds with a rejection: "Different Transaction Collision".
This behavior can be observed in the simulation test `basic_conn_split.sh`, which is only "saved" by the central doing a phy update later.

**Expected behavior**
The host app expects that at least a reasonable effort has gone into executing the auto-initiated LLCPs, doing simple retries where applicable.

**Impact**
Link is left in 1 Mbps phy when 2 is expected.

**Environment**
Issue is seen on vendor implementation based on Zephyr 2.2.1, and on latest master with CI test `basic_conn_split.sh`.
comments: Updated description to only consider "Different Transaction Collison" issue, as the "DISALLOWED" issue was fixed.

Downgrading to low because this has a very simple workaround, which is to retrigger the procedure from the application, and there are no explicit guarantees for retrial in the auto-initiated API.
I think we should create another enhancement issue covering the behavior of auto-initiated APIs when the procedure fails.

review_comments: No need for the () since what the macros expand to are "atomic" in that there's no way the parenthesis can help ensure the correct evaluation order.
That said, are these fixed values really universal, and no one would want them any different? If not, then Kconfig may be the better way.

Good question. I just wanted - as a starting point - to avoid polluting the config-space. I think the PHY_REQ_MAX_RETRY could easily be a CONFIG, maybe keeping PHY_REQ_RETRY_CI fixed, as it relates to LLCP instant.
